note: Curated narrative angles for inventory topics. An angle replaces the generic inventory title in ranking and review, never in the inventory itself. premiseStatus: VERIFIED = the title's factual premise was read in a primary source (quoted below); SUPPORTED_SECONDARY = several independent secondary sources agree, primary not read; NEEDS_RESEARCH = plausible angle whose premise has not been checked. Every angle still has to pass the research gate before scripting. rejectedTitles records wordings that were considered and why they are not accurate.

angles.workingTitle: America Stopped Making Pennies. Who Pays Now?
angles.premise: The US Mint ended circulating penny production in November 2025 after the unit cost reached 3.69 cents; cash totals are now rounded in different ways by different retailers.

evidence.claim: Final circulating penny struck at the Philadelphia Mint on 2025-11-12
evidence.source: CoinNews; KSL; Coin World (reporting the US Mint release)

evidence.claim: Unit cost 3.69 cents in 2024 (0.97 cents in 2005)
evidence.source: Mint data as cited by CoinNews

evidence.claim: Retailers round differently (Love's rounds change up; Kwik Trip rounds cash totals down); card payments unaffected

primaryToRead: congress.gov status of the Common Cents Act (reports conflict)
openQuestions: Federal rounding legislation status: sources conflict
Whether rounding nets out for consumers is a claim from a trade association (NACS), not measured data

angles.workingTitle: Half Your Movie Ticket Goes to the Studio. The Popcorn Doesn't.
angles.premise: In AMC's US markets, film exhibition costs were 51.6% of admissions revenue in 2024 while food and beverage costs were 17.3% of food and beverage revenue. Company-wide, tickets and concessions each left about $1.32 billion after their direct costs.

evidence.claim: US markets: film exhibition costs 51.6% of admissions revenues (2024); food and beverage costs 17.3% of F&B revenues
Consolidated 2024: admissions $2,560.5M, film exhibition costs $1,239.2M; food and beverage $1,624.9M, F&B costs $305.6M (our arithmetic: $1,321.3M vs $1,319.3M after direct costs)

rejectedTitles.title: Your Movie Ticket Barely Pays for the Movie
rejectedTitles.reason: overclaims: AMC keeps about 48-52% of admissions revenue after film costs

rejectedTitles.title: Why Movie Theaters Make Almost Nothing From Ticket Sales
rejectedTitles.reason: contradicted by the same 10-K (see freshness watchlist)

openQuestions: One chain; Cinemark/Regal ratios should be added for a fair industry picture

angles.workingTitle: Billions Sit on Unused Gift Cards. Who Keeps the Money?
angles.premise: Survey estimates put unused US gift card and store-credit balances in the tens of billions; companies recognise the share they expect never to be redeemed as 'breakage' revenue (Starbucks: $222.4M in fiscal 2025), subject to state unclaimed-property laws.
angles.statusNote: the mechanism (breakage) is primary-verified; the headline 'billions' rests on a survey extrapolation (Starbucks' $1.75B balance also includes loyalty Stars), so the title premise is secondary-supported

evidence.claim: Starbucks recognised breakage revenue of $200.4M (company-operated) and $22.0M (licensed) in fiscal 2025; $187.6M and $20.0M in fiscal 2024
evidence.source: Starbucks FY2025 Form 10-K, revenue recognition note

evidence.claim: Starbucks stored value cards and loyalty program liability $1,751.7M at 2025-09-28
Breakage estimates account for remittance to government agencies under unclaimed property laws
About $27B in unused gift cards, vouchers and store credit; 43% of US adults hold at least one (Sept 2024 survey)

rejectedTitles.title: The Billions Stuck on Gift Cards You Forgot
rejectedTitles.reason: the survey measures unused balances, not forgotten ones

openQuestions: Use the newest Bankrate release if one exists; the 2024 figure is a survey extrapolation, so say so on screen

angles.workingTitle: Why Your Car Wash Wants a Monthly Subscription
angles.premise: At Mister Car Wash, the largest listed US operator, Unlimited Wash Club subscriptions were 75% of wash sales in Q4 2024 with over 2.1 million members across 514 locations.

evidence.claim: UWC sales 75% of total wash sales in Q4 2024 (74% in Q4 2023); over 2.1 million members at 2024-12-31; 514 locations
evidence.source: Mister Car Wash Q4/FY2024 results, Form 8-K exhibit 99.1

evidence.claim: Private equity owns most national express-tunnel platforms; Zips Car Wash filed Chapter 11 in February 2025
evidence.source: trade and market reports (not read in full)

rejectedTitles.title: Why Car Washes Are Suddenly Everywhere
rejectedTitles.reason: no reliable count of new US car wash sites by year was found; keep it as a research question, not a title claim

openQuestions: Unit growth of express tunnels (Professional Carwashing & Detailing Top 50 list)
The Zips bankruptcy is the natural conflict beat: confirm filing details

angles.workingTitle: The Rule That Forced Hotels to Show the Real Price
angles.premise: Since 2025-05-12 the FTC fee rule requires covered lodging and live-event tickets to show the total price including mandatory fees up front; the fees themselves are still allowed.

evidence.claim: Rule effective 2025-05-12; all-in price must be most prominent; resort fees not banned

openQuestions: Any enforcement actions or litigation since 2025

angles.workingTitle: What Happened to Temu's Prices After the Loophole Closed
angles.premise: The US de minimis exemption for Chinese parcels ended in May 2025; Temu moved to US-warehouse listings and added import charges.

evidence.claim: Temu halted direct-from-China shipping and showed import charges after the exemption ended

openQuestions: Later changes to de minimis for other countries

angles.workingTitle: How Spirit Airlines Ran Out of Runway

evidence.claim: Spirit ceased all operations 2026-05-02; Chapter 11 in Nov 2024 and Aug 2025
